symptom: After a save through mxcli the next process's catalog refresh opens the saved unit file again instead of serving it from .mxcli/cache/unit-contents.db (TestCatalogRefresh_NextProcessOpensOnlyChangedUnits: 1 read, want 0)
cause: `Reader.InvalidateUnit` patches the unit cache for one written unit instead of rebuilding it; `buildUnitCache` is where the unit store learns each row's ContentsHash (`noteRowHash`/`setRowHashes`), so the patched read recorded the new bytes under the old row hash and the next process rejected them
insight: Anything that refreshes part of the unit cache must repeat what `buildUnitCache` does per unit: read through `readUnit` (not `os.ReadFile`, which skips the store) and note the row's new hash first. The store test's mxcli-save step is the only one that catches it; a write through `InvalidateCache` never shows it
